title: Actinic keratoses (solar keratoses)
summary: Rough, scaly UV-induced dysplastic patches on sun-damaged skin: a marker of field cancerisation with a small risk of SCC. Sun protection, then lesion- or field-directed treatment, and when to refer.

glance.think: Gritty, scaly, sun-exposed macules that are easier to feel than see — versus waxy “stuck-on” seborrhoeic keratoses.
glance.engine: AK: UV-driven keratinocyte dysplasia (field cancerisation). SK: benign clonal keratinocyte proliferation.
glance.backbone: Photoprotection for everyone; single AKs — cryotherapy; field change — 5-FU / imiquimod / diclofenac per local pathway; reassure on typical SKs.
glance.never_miss: Tender, enlarging, ulcerated or hypertrophic lesions — rule out SCC. Pigmented facial “lentigo” that is irregular — think lentigo maligna.

what: **Actinic keratoses (AKs)** are common UV-induced dysplastic lesions on chronically sun-exposed skin of older adults. They mark **field cancerisation** and a small risk of progression to squamous cell carcinoma.
Benign **seborrhoeic keratoses** are covered on their own page: [seborrhoeic keratosis](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis).

list: AK: cumulative UVB/UVA; fair skin, outdoor work, immunosuppression (transplant) raise burden and SCC risk.
Actinic cheilitis is AK of the lip vermilion.
AK: rough sandpaper scale on erythematous base; face, bald scalp, ears, forearms, hands; often multiple.
Hypertrophic AK and cutaneous horn need careful SCC exclusion.

diagnosis: Clinical ± dermoscopy. Biopsy or 2WW/urgent skin cancer referral if SCC or melanoma cannot be excluded. Never destroy an undiagnosed pigmented lesion with cryotherapy or laser.

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Stuck-on waxy vs gritty flat scale
Flat even brown macule — see [solar lentigines](condition:solar-lentigines)

list: Daily broad-spectrum SPF 30–50, hat, behaviour change; skin self-check education.

management.h: Lesion- and field-directed options (local formulary / CKS themes)

list: Few discrete AKs: **cryotherapy** (light freeze) in trained hands.
Field change: topical **5-fluorouracil**, **imiquimod**, **diclofenac 3% gel**, or photodynamic therapy via dermatology — expect an inflammatory treatment phase; counsel clearly.
Actinic cheilitis: lower threshold for specialist review.

red_flags: Possible SCC or melanoma → urgent suspected-cancer referral (NG12).
Rapidly enlarging tender nodule in an AK field.
Lip AK with induration or ulceration.
pearls: Feel with a fingertip — AKs are gritty.
Treating the field matters more than chasing every spot once cancer is excluded.
Warn that 5-FU/imiquimod look worse before they look better.
Tender, thickened or growing AK, or an AK on the lip or ear: see [cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma](condition:squamous-cell-carcinoma) for when it may have become SCC.
